title: Integrator 15min Ops Surge — Battlebrief (sketch)
summary: A super-short, engineer-focused slide set for sellers/SEs to run a 15-minute technical touch with integrator/SRE teams. Emphasis: immediate risk heuristics, rapid canary checklist, fallback options, and one-call migration/rollback play.
slides: Title: Integrator 15min Ops Surge — Battlebrief (sketch) — Priya/KP
Why this call matters: quick trust-building with platform engineers. Goal: 3 decisions — can we run a 1-hour pilot? can we agree on SLOs for the pilot? do we have a rollback path?
Agenda (3 parts, 15 min total): 1) 4-min environment & constraints briefing, 2) 6-min risk & canary checklist + demo data, 3) 5-min next-steps + rollback commitments
Slide: Quick contextual one-liner for integrators — Redwood equals consistent inference across hosted/dedicated/private with explicit fallback routing and KV prefix cache to cut tail cost

Slide: Typical integrator concerns (voice-of-customer bullets): network isolation, cold-start latency, burst throughput, KV cache correctness, PII handling, deterministic rollback — short answers (1-2 lines each)

Slide: Rapid capability map (ops-first view): hosted API (fast test), dedicated (predictable throughput), private (air-gapped). Include quick decision heuristic: Proof-of-value -> Hosted; Predictable SLA -> Dedicated; Regulated -> Private

Slide: Canary checklist (6 items — run in <60m): 1) Tokenize & baseline traffic sample (n=50 reqs); 2) Baseline latency vs budget (p50/p95); 3) Throughput smoke (rps for expected peak); 4) KV prefix correctness test; 5) Fallback verification (route to smaller model/regional failover); 6) Audit log & KMS smoke
Speaker note for checklist: If p95 > target, enable prefix cache and reduce batch window; if throughput insufficient, enable burst capacity or route lower-tier model

Slide: Quick tradeoffs table (ops view) — three rows: Latency, Cost per token, Predictability. Columns: Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Short bullets under each cell (e.g., Hosted: low friction, higher unit variance; Dedicated: predictable unit cost, reserved capacity; Private: complete isolation, infra ops overhead)

Slide: Fallback matrix (one-liner): Primary model -> fallback variant -> region fallback -> degrade to stateless prompt-only. Include example mapping: gpt-like-32k -> quant-8-small -> us-east-2 warm pool -> text-only stub

Slide: Sample API micro-runbook (for SRE): 1) Curl health endpoint + retry headers, 2) Check per-route token counters in Console, 3) Switch routing policy via API (body example), 4) Promote/depromote model versions. Provide sample curl snippet (conceptual)
battlecard_qna: Q: Customer wants 'no black boxes' on latency — what do we say?; A: We show deterministic profiling: kernel selection + sequence-length heatmap. Offer a 30-min profiling session with ops to produce p50/p95 by shard and by prompt length.

Q: How do we keep cost predictable during spikes?; A: Reserve Dedicated capacity for critical routes, or configure burst caps + smart fallback to a cheaper quantized variant. Redwood Optimize can suggest batch/quant profiles based on sampled traffic.
Q: What compliance evidence can we provide during pilot?; A: KMS integration proof, access logs slice, and an attestation checklist. Offer a short SOC-like smoke validation for the pilot environment.

Q: Performance regressions after update — what's the rollback path?; A: Canary traffic config (percent routing), automatic quality regression alert tied to eval set; one API call flips routing back to previous model version and promotes warm KV cache from previous pool. Provide playbook link.

Q: If integrator needs air-gap, how fast for Private?; A: Typical onboarding is 6–10 weeks for full air-gapped on-prem. For pilots, suggest VPC-hosted private control plane + local runtime for faster validation (2–4 weeks).
benchmark_snippets: Pilot baseline (example): 512-token avg prompt — hosted p50 65ms, p95 180ms; Dedicated warm pool p50 45ms, p95 110ms; quant-8 variant p95 improves 30-40% but watch hallucination delta
Cost heuristics (example): for conversational route, toggling KV prefix cache reduced token cost by ~18% in a sample fintech workload — note: depends on token reuse patterns
Throughput note: dedicated pool 4x single-host concurrency with continuous batching; if you expect sudden 10x bursts, add burst units or regional overflow routing
pilot-handoff-checklist: Business: pilot objectives + success metrics (SLOs, cost target, quality threshold)
Access: API key for pilot users, RBAC for logs & models, KMS access where needed
Telemetry: connect pilot to customer's monitoring (trace IDs, per-route token counters), short retention export
Safety: blacklist/guardrails, allowed system tools, data retention settings
Rollback: documented one-click rollback command, who has perms, expected downtime (if any)
recommended_next_steps: Book 30-min ops profiling with integrator (Priya/Aisha) — output: p50/p95 by prompt length and recommended quant/profile
Provision hosted pilot for 1 week with ingress sample traffic and monitoring hooks
Run the 6-item canary checklist with integrator on day 0 of pilot
Document agreed rollback & SLA items in Jira (GPILOT-342) and confirm team contacts
